hyps.why: Filling an empty direct input-output edge adds a new path, giving a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Adding a skip shortcut where there was none helps more than swapping one existing op for another.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is already none cuts the input's main route and causes a large drop.
With edge 5 absent, removing edge 0 leaves few paths to the output, causing a big accuracy loss.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, removing edge 0 damages the remaining paths much more.
When the direct 0->3 path is missing, a skip on edge 5 supplies a useful shortcut, unlike when it is already present.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so upgrading edge 4 gives little benefit.
In skip- or pool-dominated cells, replacing a conv on edge 2 with pooling removes the only learnable path and collapses accuracy.
Upgrading a 1x1 conv to 3x3 yields a smaller gain than upgrading from none, skip or pooling.
Without the direct 0->3 bypass, adding a heavy conv on edge 0 was the only case that reduced accuracy.
